name: Anguilla
summary: An island that rebelled against a federation—and sought a British connection.
notes: Anguilla’s 1967–1969 separation was locally effective but internationally unrecognized. It belongs on the contested/local-government lane, not among recognized sovereign states. French and Spanish raids did not establish enduring colonial governments.

events.title: The Carlisle patent
events.detail: England granted Anguilla without establishing a colony.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: English settlers arrive
events.detail: Settlers from Saint Kitts established a colony.

events.title: A French raid
events.detail: A French expedition attacked from Saint Martin; no lasting change of government followed.

events.title: Part of an associated state
events.detail: Saint Christopher-Nevis-Anguilla gained internal autonomy under Britain.

events.title: Anguilla breaks with Saint Kitts
events.detail: Islanders expelled the federation’s police and established local control.

events.title: Unrecognized independence proclaimed
events.detail: The declaration sought separation from Saint Kitts; Britain did not recognize an independent state.

events.title: British direct administration returns
events.detail: British forces landed and restored administration under emergency powers.

events.title: A separate British dependency
events.detail: Formal separation from Saint Kitts-Nevis confirmed Anguilla’s chosen British connection.
